divergences.old: dynatrace entities list, services, workloads and problems list following nextPageKey with no limit on the number of pages
divergences.toil: The same stop rule (until a page has no nextPageKey), plus a bound: after 1,000 pages (500,000 items) the command fails with HTTP, naming what was being paged, and fix text to narrow the request. A server that hands back a key it already gave also ends the loop
divergences.why: A server that kept returning a nextPageKey would otherwise be asked for pages forever.

divergences.old: Named environments as dynatrace.environments.<name>.{baseUrl, apiToken, platformUrl, platformToken} beside flat dynatrace.* keys, with dynatrace.defaultEnvironment picking one when --env was absent; an unknown name failed with a fix naming dynatrace.environments.<name>.baseUrl
divergences.toil: Each environment is a dynatrace connection. --env selects the connection named <name>, or the one whose env setting is <name>; defaults.dynatrace.connection takes the place of defaultEnvironment, and keys every environment shares go under defaults.dynatrace, below each connection's own. An unknown --env is INVALID_INPUT listing the environments toil knows
divergences.why: toil's config is a set of named connections, and --env is the one environment concept that selects among them (decision 9 on #68), so it can't be a nested map inside one connection. The unknown-name error lists the valid ones, as decision 9 requires.

divergences.old: With dynatrace.defaultEnvironment set, the stored environment's baseUrl, apiToken, platformUrl and platformToken won over the DYNATRACE_* env vars, which only filled fields the environment left out, also for an environment picked with --env (#83 item 6)
divergences.toil: TOIL_DYNATRACE_* env vars configure the default connection and win over anything stored for it. Another connection takes only its own TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_* variables, then defaults.dynatrace; the TOIL_DYNATRACE_* token never fills a gap in it
divergences.why: Env vars outrank every stored value, and a credential goes only to the connection it's configured on. The predecessor could send a CI job's token to a stored environment's host.
